summary: The court of Versailles, built by Louis XIV from the 1660s to trap France's nobility in ruinous etiquette, gambling and intrigue, drained the treasury and, under Louis XV, cut the crown off from Parisians, feeding the road to revolution.

evidence.note: Host frames the system and nobility of Versailles, not one person, as the bastard
Louis XIV's 1638 birth and childhood under the regency are narrated at length
Fronde civil war of judges and nobles against the regency, about 8 minutes; root of Versailles
Mazarin dies in 1661 and the Fouquet party prompts the Versailles project
Tens of thousands of builders worked in deadly conditions; bodies removed at night
Court trade in charms, black masses and poisons to win the king's favour
Police investigation and Burning Chamber tribunal of 1679 over poisoners
Long segment on Paris news ecosystem: newsmongers, libels, gossip songs
War of Austrian Succession: costly Lawfeld battle, unpopular peace and war taxes
Louis XV's silent reception at Notre Dame in 1751 is the last event covered at length

notes: Louis XIV dominates both parts but the host names the Versailles system as the bastard, so the palace/court is primary (place) and Louis XIV secondary; with a place primary, roles stay empty. Covered span ends 1751; Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette and 1789 are only previewed. Modern Trump/Musk oligarchy framing treated as commentary, not reaches_present.
